      <section id="welcome" class="welcome-section">

          <h1>Welcome to AffineDrift</h1>
          <p class="subtitle">Control Theory and Multibody Dynamics Applied to the Golf Swing</p>
        </div>

        <div class="welcome-intro">
          <p>
            AffineDrift applies control theory and multibody dynamics to the biomechanics of the golf swing. This site collects research notes, textbook chapters, and curated resources for researchers and engineers interested in the intersection of robotics, biomechanics, and sport science.
          </p>
          <p>
            The material is organized into two textbooks, a collection of standalone articles, and a curated resource library of external references.
          </p>
        </div>
      </section>



      <!-- Math Showcase -->
      <section id="framework" class="math-section">
        <h2>The Core Framework</h2>
        <p>The golf swing can be modeled as a control-affine system:</p>
        <div class="math-showcase">
          $$\dot{x} = f(x) + g(x)u$$
        </div>
        <p>
          Where <em>f(x)</em> represents the drift dynamics (passive forces like gravity and centrifugal effects) and <em>g(x)u</em> represents the controlled torque inputs from the golfer.
        </p>
        <div style="margin-top: 1rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; background: var(--bg-secondary, #f8f9fa); border-left: 3px solid var(--primary-color, #2563eb); border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-light, #6b7280);">
          <strong>Provenance:</strong> The control-affine form ẋ = f(x) + g(x)u is standard in nonlinear control theory (Isidori, 1995; Nijmeijer &amp; van der Schaft, 1990). Its application to golf biomechanics — the drift/input decomposition, ZTCF, and DCR — is AffineDrift synthesis. See the <a href="articles/theory-part1.html">Theory Part 1</a> derivation and the <a href="critiques/index.html">Critiques &amp; Responses</a> for scope limitations.
        </div>
      </section>

      <!-- About the Approach Section -->
      <section id="approach" class="approach-section">
        <h2>Research Methodology</h2>
        <div class="approach-content">
          <p>
            This site uses AI-assisted content generation with iterative human review. Articles and topics are outlined by the author, then developed with AI assistance and refined through multiple review cycles. The emphasis is on producing verifiable mathematical expressions, reviewable code, and traceable source references rather than unconstrained text generation.
          </p>
          <p>
            Rather than asking it for answers, ask it to provide mathematical expressions that can be validated. Ask it to write code that can be reviewed. Ask it to track down sources and links for further information.
          </p>
          <p>
            The review process employs specialized AI agents with distinct roles: editorial review for prose quality, curation for topic development, bibliography management for cross-linked references, and mathematical validation for equation verification.
          </p>
          <p>
            Importantly, there are also critics. My goal here is not to hide weakness, but identify it and explore it. The edge cases and shortcomings of a given paradigm often hold extreme value.
          </p>
        </div>
      </section>
